timing: 45-minute version: 5 minutes for arrival coloring, 8 minutes for the shared story spark, 17 minutes for drafting, 5 minutes for decorating, and 10 minutes for group share.
60-minute version: 10 minutes for arrival table work, 10 minutes for the adult-led quest launch, 20 minutes for station drafting, 10 minutes for covers, and 10 minutes for take-home folders.
75-minute version: 10 minutes for arrival, 12 minutes for warm-up choices, 25 minutes for rotating story stations, 13 minutes for extension activity, and 15 minutes for optional sentence sharing.
For a classroom celebration, run the story spark before treats, then use cake or snack time as the natural break before folders go home.
Keep a visible timer at the adult seat and announce the last 3 minutes before each move so children can finish a sentence instead of stopping mid-thought.
tableSetup: Cover one main table with plain craft paper and place a pencil cup, crayons, scissors, tape, and a small scrap-paper tray in the center.
Set one folder or envelope per child with a story map, draft page, cover page, and blank ending card already stacked in use order.
Use color dots or table numbers for groups instead of personal data labels, and keep the host copy beside the timer.
Put four station signs around the table: place, helper, mix-up, and ending, with enough printed choice cards for two children to use each station at once.
Keep snacks, drinks, candles, and gift bags on a separate surface so the writing pages stay dry and easy to send home.
adultScript: No scary harm, no bullying, no romance, no weapons, no branded characters, no real child profiles.
Today we are making tiny quest stories. You can point, draw, dictate to an adult, or write your own words.
A good party story needs one clear place, one helpful character, one small mix-up, and one kind ending.
If you get stuck, choose between the two cards in front of you, then say the sentence out loud before writing.
For sharing, you may read one sentence, ask an adult to read one sentence, show a drawing, or pass and be a careful listener.
takeHomePrep: Before guests arrive, print one complete packet per child plus three spare packets for siblings, mistakes, or late additions.
Pre-fold each cover page and tuck the story map inside so children leave with a finished booklet shape even if the draft is short.
Add one blank thank-you note sheet behind the story page for families who want to turn the quest into a later note.
At the end, place loose choice cards in a small envelope inside each folder so the story can be finished at home without extra setup.

partyRoutines.name: Arrival Quest Table
partyRoutines.bestFor: The first 10 minutes while guests arrive at different times.
steps: Place one low-pressure map or cover page at every seat before the first child arrives.
Invite each child to color, circle a favorite place, or add one label while waiting for the group.
Ask an adult helper to quietly slide finished arrival pages into the child's folder.
Begin the main quest once most seats are filled, using the arrival page as the first story detail.

partyRoutines.name: Story Station Carousel
partyRoutines.bestFor: A 60-minute party with 8-16 children and two adult helpers.
steps: Set four stations around one table: place card, helper card, mix-up card, and ending card.
Start each group at a different station and give them 4 minutes to circle or write one choice.
Rotate groups clockwise until each folder has one note from every station.
Bring everyone back to seats and turn the four notes into a short draft or dictated story.

partyRoutines.name: Whole-Group Quest Build
partyRoutines.bestFor: Library tables, classroom celebrations, or younger groups that need one shared pace.
steps: Read the quest starter aloud and hold up two printable choices at a time.
Let the group choose by pointing to the left or right side of the table.
Write the group choice on a large sheet, then have each child copy, sketch, or adapt it on their own page.
Repeat for place, helper, mix-up, and ending so every child leaves with a complete story frame.

partyRoutines.name: Pair-and-Polish Mini Draft
partyRoutines.bestFor: Older children, homeschool co-ops, and classroom groups with 20 minutes of focused writing time.
steps: Give pairs one story map and ask each child to choose one different detail to add.
Set a 7-minute quiet draft timer while adults help with spelling only when asked.
Have partners trade pages and underline one detail that is already clear.
Ask each child to add one stronger noun, action, or sound before the group share.

partyRoutines.name: Take-Home Quest Folder Finish
partyRoutines.bestFor: Busy birthday parties where writing must fit between treats, photos, and free play.
steps: Run only the story spark and first draft page during the party.
Use a folder checklist with three boxes: map started, sentence started, ending chosen.
Let children decorate the cover while adults gather pages and loose cards.
Send the folder home with a one-step finish note: add one ending sentence after the party.

extensionActivities.title: Invitation Map Warm-Up
extensionActivities.direction: Children draw a tiny route from the party door to an invented quest table, then label three stops with ordinary details from the room.

extensionActivities.title: Snack Table Sensory List
extensionActivities.direction: Before snacks are served, children list one color, one shape, one sound, and one texture they can borrow for a story scene.

extensionActivities.title: Gift-Bow Character Choice
extensionActivities.direction: Give each child a paper bow shape and ask them to write two helpful choices a character could make with it in a tiny quest.

extensionActivities.title: Table Tent Quest Titles
extensionActivities.direction: Fold blank cards into table tents and have children write a story title on the front and three clue words on the back.

extensionActivities.title: Kind Ending Spinner
extensionActivities.direction: Use a paper spinner with three ending types: help someone, fix a mix-up, or learn a useful lesson, then write one matching final sentence.

extensionActivities.title: Three-Prop Story Sort
extensionActivities.direction: Place three safe everyday props on the table and ask groups to sort them into place detail, helpful item, or ending clue.

extensionActivities.title: Thank-You Note Story Bridge
extensionActivities.direction: Children draft one thank-you sentence that mentions an invented quest detail, then add one real appreciation sentence for the host.

extensionActivities.title: Table Gallery Walk
extensionActivities.direction: Finished pages stay on the table while children walk quietly, place one star sticker beside a clear detail, and return to revise one line.

groupShareCards: Read one sentence you are proud of, then tell the group which word you chose carefully.
Point to one map or cover detail and explain where the character goes next.
Ask an adult to read one line for you while you hold up the page.
Tell the group which choice card helped your story most: place, helper, mix-up, or ending.
Ask listeners to choose one detail you could add next: color, sound, action, or feeling.
Pass today and take the listener job: notice one clear detail from another child's story.
